prompt: Four numbers have mean $10$. Three of them are $8, 11, 9$. What is the fourth?
hint: The mean and the count together tell you what all four numbers must add up to.

hints.title: 🔁 Another angle
hints.text: Try two numbers first: if two numbers have mean $10$ and one of them is $8$, what total must they share?
The mean and the count together tell you what all four numbers must add up to.
The four numbers total $4 \times 10 = 40$. The three known numbers add to $8 + 11 + 9 = 28$, so find what is left.

explanation: The total equals the mean times the count, so the four numbers add to $4 \times 10 = 40$.
The three known numbers add to $8 + 11 + 9 = 28$.
The fourth number is whatever is left of the total: $40 - 28 = 12$.
The fourth number is $12$, and checking, $(8 + 11 + 9 + 12) \div 4 = 10$.
